# Gabe / Guy
Date: 2026-08-19 | Duration: 48m

## Summary
The team discussed enhancing the SDK onboarding process by prioritizing AI-assisted setup as the default while keeping manual options available. Key topics included potential UI improvements for clarity and usability, including the introduction of a persistent notification banner for incomplete SDK setups. They confirmed that the SDK connection is established post-AI script execution. The importance of clear metadata presentation through data tables was highlighted to avoid overwhelming users. Prototype sharing methods were also discussed for improved collaboration, along with the removal of confetti animation to adhere to accessibility standards.

## Keywords
AI-assisted setup, SDK connection, prototype collaboration, onboarding flow, organizational selector, accessibility animation

## Action Items

**Gabe Melean**
Update copy for "invite your developer" to a more generic term to accommodate broader user roles (02:40)
Experiment with UI flow changes regarding SDK language selection, testing it as either a first step or nested under AI-assisted setup (11:00)
Remove the "skip" button from the SDK connection checking page except in the footer and test the adjusted flow (12:55)
Demonstrate the AI setup and authorization flow within the prototype reflecting the current backend process (15:45)
Remove confetti animation from setup UI due to accessibility concerns (20:10)
Implement data table layout for the summary page, refining metadata presentation with input from Guy Langford-lee (21:40)
Adjust links on the summary page to show new tab icon and confirm they open in a new tab (25:09)
Handle the presence of "what’s next" blocks at different UI points, considering homepage versus setup page redundancy (27:02)
Implement a persistent notification banner for SDK connection setup reminders on relevant pages using the existing Radix component (28:57)
Incorporate the "what you created" content into the SDK connection details page for better discoverability (31:30)
Tag items created by the Growth Book wizard for contextual identification within the UI (33:40)
Limit AI-assisted setup display by language support and remove it when AI assist is not available (36:45)
Update prototype based on feedback including renaming invite copy and adjusting UI elements, then finalize handoff for sharing and collaboration environment (37:10)
Look into GitHub access and repository permissions needed for deployment of the prototype and request access from Jeremy (37:55)

**Guy Langford-lee**
Assist Gabe in pushing prototype code to a branch and guide on repository usage and testing (36:59)
Review existing authorization product flow and confirm or suggest adjustments (19:07)
Explore the organizational selector behavior for multi-organization versus single-organization users and confirm UI logic (17:15)
Validate removal of confetti animation and discuss its impact focusing on accessibility (20:40)
Provide insight into attribute types, enums, and source metadata to refine data table approach for summary page (22:40)
Check existing Radix component usability for persistent SDK connection notification banner (29:07)
Test behavior of "exit setup" leading to homepage to ensure visibility of next steps for the user (27:20)
Help scope and prioritize adding AI-assisted setup to SDK connection page versus incremental rollout (35:15)
Communicate with Jeremy to facilitate Gabe’s access to GitHub and internal repositories (38:00)

# Gabe / Guy
Date: 2026-10-14 | Duration: 15.15999984741211m

## Summary
The team planned clearer review categories for “Needs Your Review,” “Needs Another Look,” and “Your Reviews,” with nested tabs or stateful table-header buttons to manage large review sets. Gabe and Guy agreed to work in parallel, with Gabe refining the interface and Guy building backend support for filtering, comments, scalable lists, and request navigation. They also aligned on a reusable system-level details page for experiments and features, using a clean layout with core content on the left and dynamic comments and metadata in a right rail. Titles, descriptions, and rollout rules may support inline or modal editing. For the Anthropics presentation, the focus will be a clean interface, dynamic publish status, comments, and a cautious presentation of robot-assisted summaries alongside a manual summary. The current design is sufficient for the presentation, with further iteration planned afterward.

## Keywords
UI design, review workflow, Anthropic meeting, right rail layout, inline editing, reusable details page

## Action Items

**Guy Langford-lee**
Prepare presentation materials reflecting discussed UI and review workflow improvements for Anthropic meeting tomorrow morning (00:00)
Separate title and description more clearly on the page and begin backend development to support new UI (03:14)
Review and iterate on design files that Gabe will send, adapting them to backend and UI refinement (13:44)

**Gabe Melean**
Send Guy the design using right rail and inline header actions, noting which parts are deprioritized and need ignoring (04:40)
Continue working on the redesign and review integration features, including navigation between review requests, and notify Guy when ready for review (06:46)
Share design PR from main repo with Guy for review and collaboration (11:32)
Provide availability for questions and support before the Anthropic meeting (13:44)
